title: Nexus and P.L. 86-272 — Lumen Furniture
instructions: Lumen Furniture, based in State A, sells furniture to customers in State B. Decide whether each set of facts keeps Lumen protected from State B net income tax under P.L. 86-272.

rows.label: Salespeople visit State B only to solicit orders, which are approved in State A and shipped from there
rows.explanation: Solicitation of orders for tangible goods approved and shipped from outside the state is protected.

rows.label: The same salespeople also collect past-due accounts in State B
Lumen keeps a stock of furniture in a State B warehouse to fill orders
rows.explanation: Inventory in the state exceeds protected activity.

rows.label: Lumen sends designers into State B to provide paid interior design services
rows.explanation: Services aren't sales of tangible personal property.

rows.label: State B asks Lumen to collect sales tax because its in-state sales exceed $300,000
rows.explanation: P.L. 86-272 applies only to net income taxes, not sales tax.
